newsitem.title: RWANDA: General says Zaire force could play airdrop role.
newsitem.headline: General says Zaire force could play airdrop role.

text.p: The Canadian general commanding a multinational force for central Africa has met rebels and aid agencies in eastern Zaire and declared that his force could play a role making emergency airdrops of food supplies.

Lieutenant-General Maurice Baril also told reporters on Sunday in the Rwandan capital Kigali that the rebels assured him that aid agencies would have access to any Rwandan refugees in need, whenever and wherever possible.

The United Nations approved the multinational force after more than one million Rwandans scattered from refugee camps in Zaire because of fighting between the rebels, government forces and Rwandan Hutu militiamen among the refugees.
More than 600,000 refugees have since gone home. Those too frightened to follow suit have wandered off through Zaire living off the land, some dying of malaria and fatigue.
Baril said he went 48 km (30 miles) into Zaire, where he learned that large groups of Rwandan refugees had broken up.
"They are still in the countryside. They have split into small groups and gone off road into the forest. We hope they'll come out of the forest and onto the road," he said.
"The nature is so luxuriant in that place...these people are certainly not in good condition, but they seem to be living off the land like so many thousands and thousands of Zairois," he added.
The general said he found the rebel-held area more secure than when he visited the town of Goma early this month.
"But there's still a lot of conflict going on and we expect the humanitarians (U.N. and other agencies) will have trouble reaching people because of the conflict," he added.

Pressed on whether his force had a role to play, he said: "We will certainly take into consideration everything. I will discuss all this with the humanitarian agencies. We will certainly make recommendations."
Later he said: "If the humanitarians found a critical situation on the ground that needs immediate help, then I would be ready to do airdrops."

Many aid agency workers are scathing about the inactivity of the multinational force, which has set up headquarters in the Ugandan capital Kampala but cannot deploy in eastern Zaire for political and security reasons.
The rebels, known as the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, do not want the force in their area in case it helps bring back the Zairean government.
The project looked doomed when a minister in the French government, one of the most active advocates, was quoted as saying he did not think it was viable.
But the French foreign ministry indicated on Sunday that Paris still favoured the international military force.

"The Ministry of Foreign Affairs wishes to underline that France's position on the implementing of United Nations resolutions about Zaire has not changed, notably concerning the deployment of a multinational force," a communique said.
On the ground in northeastern Zaire, local officials said the rebels had taken two crossroad towns, cutting the route between Bunia town and the city of Kisangani.

Bunia, said to have a garrison of 5,000 Zairean troops, is the rebels' next target as they fight towards Kisangani, the regional capital. The rebels say they want to march on Kinshasa and overthrow President Mobutu Sese Seko, who is in France recovering from cancer surgery.
